messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The bug report mentions that `HelpFormatter#setOptionComparator(null)` does not display values in the inserted order, which contradicts the expected behavior of displaying options in the order they were inserted when no comparator is set.

The failing test `testOptionComparatorInsertedOrder` fetches the collection of `Option`s from `getOptions().getOptions()` and verifies that the options are returned in the exact insertion order stored in `insertedOrder`.

Inspection of the `HelpFormatter.setOptionComparator()` method shows it simply sets a `optionComparator` field, presumably used later for sorting options. The relevant method for fetching options is `Options.getOptions()`, which returns an unmodifiable collection of `helpOptions()`. The `helpOptions()` method returns a new list constructed from the values of `shortOpts` map: `return new ArrayList<Option>(shortOpts.values());`.

The insertion order of options appears to depend on the iteration order of `shortOpts.values()`. If `shortOpts` is not an insertion-ordered map (like LinkedHashMap), but a plain HashMap, then the order of values returned will not reflect the insertion order.

Looking at `Options.addOption(Option)`, we see that options are added to `shortOpts` map keyed by their option keys, but the map implementation is not shown here. If `shortOpts` is a HashMap, then the iteration order of values is undefined, so `getOptions()` will not return options in insertion order.

In summary, when `HelpFormatter.setOptionComparator(null)` disables the comparator, options are expected to be displayed in insertion order, but the use of a HashMap for `shortOpts` causes iteration in an arbitrary order, breaking this invariant. The root cause is that `Options.getOptions()` depends on a map whose value iteration order is not insertion-ordered.

Hence, the bug arises from the implementation of `Options.getOptions()` and the underlying storage structure of options (the `shortOpts` map) not preserving insertion order, which breaks the display order contract when no comparator is set in `HelpFormatter`.

Suggested fixed locations would involve ensuring the option collection returned by `Options.getOptions()` respects insertion order, either by changing `shortOpts` to a `LinkedHashMap` or modifying `getOptions()` or `HelpFormatter` to apply ordering.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
